title: Salad spinner
prompt: A labelled scale teaching model of the page 39 salad spinner has a hand-driven outer gear ring, the pictured intermediate planet gear and small central sun gear driving a perforated basket inside a collecting bowl. The teaching model holds the intermediate gear axis fixed in the lid so the ring input determines the sun output; identify this mounting constraint as part of the adaptation. Spin turns the ring and shows the sun and basket rotate faster through the meshing gears. Stop drive removes the hand input and lets the basket coast down. Empty bowl pours out water collected outside the basket after the drive has stopped. See-through shows the ring's internal teeth, planet and sun teeth, their real shaft supports, basket and collecting bowl. Do not substitute a pull cord, pump, brake or generic direct drive. Rotation and water-motion arrows are overlays.
blurb: A hand-cranked ring drives a faster basket through one planet and sun gear in a teaching model whose planet axis is fixed to the lid.
adaptation: Fixed planet axis in the lid, illustrative 64:24:16 tooth counts and 120 ml wet load; manual lid lifting and bowl tipping are teaching actions, not concealed mechanisms. One planet only. No brake, freewheel, pump or pull cord.

identity.note: Gears and Belts / Salad Spinner, page 39 in both editions. The checked 2016 image labels gear ring, planet gear and sun gear.
identity.mechanism: A large internally toothed ring drives a planet or intermediate spur gear, which drives a small central sun gear and basket at greater speed. Water separates from the leaves and collects outside the basket.
identity.classificationNote: Only The Wheel and Axle and Gears and Belts are main principle chapters in this unit. Other entries are named examples, diagrams or subsection headings. Greek Mill has both historical context and a named mechanism diagram.

adaptationDecision.reason: Retain. Existing sharpener uses cutters orbiting a pencil against a fixed ring gear. This spinner uses a ring input and sun output for basket speed increase. Washer spinning has a different motor-and-drum drive. Any overlap is the water-separation principle, not the complete mechanism.
adaptationDecision.boundary: Catalog and figure metadata establish intended scope only. No existing figure runtime was certified.

prompt.note: The original omits the specific epicyclic train, allowing a generic spinner to miss the chapter's mechanism. Stop should cease driving and let motion slow unless an actual brake is separately supported. Drain should be a manual bowl-emptying action rather than an invented pump.
prompt.apparatusRelation: Named gear-driven spinner with staged wet specimens. Follow the source's depicted ring-to-planet-to-sun arrangement; do not assume every commercial planetary-spinner variant has the same connections. The restrained intermediate-gear axis is an explicit teaching-model constraint, not a newly verified claim about every commercial spinner.
